extracted.intended_audience: electric cooperative leaders, policymakers, and stakeholders concerned with grid reliability and rulemakings (EPA/DOE/FERC)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy positions to inform notice-and-comment comments on EPA/DOE rulemakings affecting power plants, permitting, and grid reliability—emphasizing technology readiness, statutory authority, timelines, and permitting reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate demonstration of technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal hinges on the widespread adoption of nascent technologies: clean hydrogen and carbon capture and storage. While both technologies are promising, they are not yet widespread or commercially available and have not been 'adequately demonstrated' as required by the Clean Air Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether EPA's relied-upon technologies are commercially available and 'adequately demonstrated' under the Clean Air Act; include evidence of commercialization status, pilot/commercial deployments, costs, and timelines when arguing feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority / major questions doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal violates the Clean Air Act by giving the EPA vast new authority of major economic and political significance without a clear statement from Congress. This disregards the 'major questions doctrine' and is inconsistent with the text, structure, and context of Clean Air Act Section 111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and document whether the rule exceeds EPA's statutory authority; argue for a clear congressional authorization if the rule imposes sweeping economic/political obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic and achievable timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rules contain timelines that are unrealistic and unachievable. The compliance deadlines endanger new and existing natural gas plants and all but ensure coal units will opt to shut down by 2035. The requisite infrastructure cannot be expected to be in place due to cost, supply chain challenges, permitting, public opposition, land ownership/access, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge compliance deadlines with concrete evidence of infrastructure, supply chain, permitting, land, and public-opposition constraints; propose realistic alternative timelines supported by reliability and deployment capacity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve reliability and affordability
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rules threaten reliability and affordability. EPA’s proposal is characterized as 'unrealistic, unachievable, and will reduce key generating resources just as Americans are increasing their reliance on electricity,' leading to more blackouts, higher costs, and greater uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how rule requirements would affect dispatchable capacity, reserve margins, system reliability metrics, and consumer costs; request reliability and affordability be an express, prioritized metric in rulemaking decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all energy sources in policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawmakers must support policies that include all energy sources to maintain reliability and affordability. 'Rolling blackouts cannot become the new normal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for technology-neutral or portfolio-based policies that preserve always-available resources (e.g., coal, natural gas, nuclear, hydro) alongside renewables and storage; document the reliability roles of each resource type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increasing demand from electrification
rubrics_metrics.description: Increasing demand for electricity as other sectors of the economy are electrified is one of the five issues currently impacting reliable delivery of electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing rules, account for projected load growth from electrification (transportation, buildings, industry) and ensure planning and timelines accommodate future demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decreasing supply due to disorderly retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decreasing electricity supply due to the disorderly retirement and insufficient replacement of existing generation is a top factor jeopardizing reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data on announced and forced retirements and realistic replacement schedules; argue that rules should avoid accelerating retirements without replacement capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting delays impede infrastructure deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting delays that prevent new electric infrastructure from being built and connected to the grid are a major reliability constraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document average permitting timelines and how they interact with compliance deadlines; recommend permitting reforms or adjusted timelines to ensure projects can be permitted and built.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply chain challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply chain challenges are limiting the ability to deploy required equipment and infrastructure in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supply-chain evidence (domestic production capacity, lead times, supplier market share) in comments to argue feasibility or request mitigation measures (e.g., phased compliance, procurement support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas availability concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems with natural gas availability (fuel security, pipeline constraints) are among the key issues affecting reliable electricity delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess regional natural gas deliverability, winter/summer fuel-security risks, and how rule timelines might exacerbate fuel-availability issues; recommend safeguards or exemptions where fuel risk is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA BSER performance standards and technology mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA identifies 'best system of emission reduction' (BSER) measures including: co-firing with natural gas, using clean hydrogen in place of natural gas, and installing carbon capture and storage (CCS). For existing coal units planning to operate after 2039, EPA would require CCS with 90% effectiveness by 2030. Existing large natural gas plants are expected to install 90% effective CCS by 2035 or co-fire with 30% low‑carbon hydrogen beginning in 2032 and almost entirely hydrogen by 2038. New natural gas plants are categorized by operating profile with differing hydrogen/CCS/co-fire requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize the technical and economic feasibility of each BSER approach and timeline; provide operational, cost, and supply evidence to contest or seek modification of specific BSER requirements and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders urged EPA to extend its comment period beyond July 24 to give those affected more time to review the long, complicated rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request formal extension of the comment period and justify with the rule’s length/complexity and the need for stakeholder analysis (legal, technical, reliability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time for independent reliability assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient time for reliability assessments by the North American Electric Reliability Corp. (NERC) and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask EPA to delay final action until NERC and regional entities can complete formal reliability assessments and for those findings to be incorporated into the final rulemaking analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-business impact assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold an official small-business panel to assess the impact of the proposed rule on small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request Small Business Administration or formal small-business panels/studies to evaluate cost and operational impacts on smaller utilities and vendors and include findings in the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA permitting time limits (two-year EIS / one-year EA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting reforms: environmental impact statements must be done within two years and less intensive environmental assessments must be completed within a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose statutory or regulatory deadlines for NEPA processes to provide project certainty while preserving rigorous review; cite average EIS durations (e.g., 4.5 years) as justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater applicant involvement in permitting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Greater applicant involvement in the process: member-owned co-ops 'know the specific details of their projects and the unique needs and challenges facing their communities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate procedural reforms that increase applicant participation (data-sharing, scoping, mitigation planning) to reduce delays and improve review relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient reviews for recurring small projects
rubrics_metrics.description: More efficient reviews for recurring small projects—such as trimming trees to prevent power outages and wildfires—that are known to have minimal environmental impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request categorical exclusions or streamlined processes for routine, low-impact activities to reduce administrative burden and accelerate critical maintenance work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit lengthy, costly litigation that delays projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit lengthy, costly litigation that can delay projects indefinitely. 'Litigation can result in excessive paperwork and unnecessary delays—holding up projects that communities badly need.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose mechanisms to reduce frivolous or excessive litigation (e.g., standing reforms, time-limited challenges, judicial deference to agency NEPA decisions) balanced with protecting valid legal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-agency use of categorical exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: If one agency develops a 'categorical exclusion' from certain rules for a specific type of project, another agency can use that same exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage harmonization of categorical exclusions across agencies to shorten duplicative review where environmental impacts are well-understood and minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited permitting for large energy storage projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The reforms create an expedited permitting process for large energy storage projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support expedited pathways for storage where appropriate, but ensure expedited review retains key environmental protections and considers siting/reliability tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission permitting and siting improvements reflecting co-op/community needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that transmission permitting and siting improvements reflect co-op and community needs. 'The electric grid needs more electric grid transmission capacity to meet expected growth in the coming decades.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend stakeholder-informed reforms to siting/permitting that balance national/transmission planning with local co-op/community priorities and minimize delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not expand FERC authority over electric co-ops
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies to spur additional capacity must not expand the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s authority over electric co-ops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing federal permitting or reliability reforms, request explicit protections for the statutory autonomy of member-owned co-ops where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mandating materials that exacerbate supply-chain risk (transformer amorphous steel rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Senators urged DOE to refrain from promulgating a transformer standard that would require amorphous steel, which has only one domestic supplier and could exacerbate transformer shortages and supply-chain delays up to two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue against material mandates that strain limited domestic supplier capacity; propose phased approaches, dual-material allowances (GOES and amorphous steel coexisting), and stakeholder convenings to develop consensus-based standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize domestic electrical steel production and supply-chain resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: NRECA and allied organizations urged the White House to prioritize domestic electrical steel production (GOES and NOES) to meet demand for electrification, grid modernization, and distribution transformers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request federal actions (summits, procurement guarantees, incentives) to bolster domestic GOES/NOES production and reduce reliance on scarce foreign supply to support reliability and project timelines.
